topic: Distance, Displacement, Speed, Velocity, and Acceleration
key_concepts: Distance is the length of the path traveled.
Displacement is the straight-line change from initial to final position with direction.
Distance is a scalar quantity with magnitude only.
Displacement is a vector quantity with magnitude and direction.
Displacement can be positive, negative, or zero depending on direction relative to initial
An object that starts and ends at the same spot has zero displacement.
Speed is a scalar quantity equal to total distance per unit time.
Velocity is a vector quantity equal to displacement per unit time.
Formula triangles can rearrange speed or velocity equations to solve for distance, time, o
Uniform motion covers equal distances in equal time intervals.
Non-uniform motion covers unequal distances in equal time intervals.
